field_key_note: D6 is ratified (2026-08-21, _CONTRACT.md rule 8, DECISION-BRIEF.md): the stored academic key is `subject`; `course` is the design's prose for the same concept and survives inside quotations only. design_cites.quote: BUSIB 4300 becomes a course fact only when the engine finds a course-code pattern together with academic context such as “syllabus,” “lecture,” “credits,” “instructor,” or “semester.”
course-code patterns that are actually ZIP codes or device models
A file named HW 3.pdf may contain only equations and the phrase “Homework 3,”

rules: **Context is required on every entry, with no exception.** A match with no catalogue-01 context term in the surrounding window produces no fact and one `unresolved` row with reason `context_check_failed` (P6 SPEC). There is no such thing as a context-free course-code entry in this file, and check.py asserts the flag on every row.
**This is a format list, not a course list.** No entry names a real course, department, or university. Values auto-create at runtime (00 §3.12); formats are the authored half.

**The stoplist is load-bearing, and it exists because context is not enough.** A genuinely academic document can contain course-code-shaped strings that are not courses: a quality-management syllabus cites ISO 9001 beside the word 'syllabus'; a tax pack mentions FORM 1040 beside 'credits'. `dept_stoplist` names letter blocks that never open a course candidate even when context terms are present. It is a list of strings, not a threshold.

**Case-sensitivity is a defense, not a style choice.** Case-insensitive matching would admit `March 2010`, `June 2024` (month + year) and ordinary words as department blocks. The cost — lowercase course codes in filenames (`phys1401_hw3.pdf`) are missed — is recorded as an uncertain row, not silently absorbed.

**Arbitration with catalogue 04 (camera filenames).** The DCF basename shape (four uppercase alphanumerics + four digits) is refused as a camera pattern in catalogue 04 precisely because it is exactly the shape of an attached course code. The reciprocal rule here: in the `filename` zone, a string whose whole-filename match is claimed by a catalogue-04 camera pattern is not simultaneously a course-code candidate. Camera-prefix blocks (DSC, DSCF, DSCN, PICT, CIMG, IMGP) are additionally stoplisted so `DSCF1234` never opens a candidate in any zone.

**Ranking still applies.** Passing pattern + context makes a candidate `validated`-eligible, not written: §3.7's ranked candidates with injected minimum score and margin still run (the design requires both), and the positional difference between a course code in a reference list and the same code in a page-one heading is carried by P6's positional weights over P4 zones.
**No numbers.** Regex quantifier bounds ({2,5}, {3,4}) are the pattern's shape, not decision thresholds; no entry carries a score, weight, or window.

entries.rationale: The design's own value: BUSIB 4300. Registrar conventions across US/CA/AU/UK institutions use a 2–5 letter subject code plus a 3–4 digit number, optionally suffixed with letters (honors/lab/writing sections: `MATH 2010W`, `CHEM 1210L`). Five-digit numbers exist (Notre Dame — verified, RESEARCH.md) but are rare and collide with ZIP codes, so {3,4} is the authored shape and the 5-digit extension is an uncertain row. Three-digit forms (`CS 152`, `PHYS 101`) are ubiquitous.
entries.false_friends: state + ZIP (`MA 02139` — excluded by shape: five digits), device models (`XPS 13` — excluded: two digits; `RTX 4090` — matches and must die at the context check or margin; A03's own case), flight numbers (`UA 1234`), all-caps months (`JUNE 2024` — stoplisted), seasons (`FALL 2025` — stoplisted), standards (`ISO 9001` — stoplisted), forms (`FORM 1040` — stoplisted), pull requests (`PR 1234` — not stoplisted because PR is a plausible department; documented residual risk)
entries.source: Notre Dame registrar course-numbering page (verified, RESEARCH.md); the 2–5-letter + 3–4-digit convention is a general-knowledge anchor recorded there

entries.pattern_label: department block attached to course number (DEPT1234)
entries.rationale: The attached form is standard in the UK (`COMP0034` UCL), Australia (`COMP1511` UNSW), and in informal US usage and filenames (`PHYS1401`, the design's grouping example). This is the single most dangerous shape in the file: it is exactly JEITA CP-3461's DCF camera basename form, which catalogue 04 refuses for the mirror-image reason. Context requirement, the camera-prefix stoplist rows, and the filename-zone arbitration rule carry the defense together.
entries.design_cite: 00 §4.3 (PHYS1401 appears attached throughout the grouping walkthrough)
entries.false_positive_risk: high without context, medium with (filename zone)
entries.false_friends: DCF camera basenames (`DSCF1234`, `PICT0001` — stoplisted prefixes + catalogue-04 arbitration), flight numbers (`UA1234`, `QF0012`), GPU/product SKUs (`RTX4090` — context check), Apple model numbers (`A2338` — excluded: one letter), airline booking refs (`ABC123` — three digits, matches; context check carries it)
entries.source: JEITA CP-3461 via catalogue 04; UNSW/UCL course-code conventions (RESEARCH.md)

entries.rationale: Named by the dispatch as a format to catalogue. Research found no confirmed registrar system that writes number-dot-department in this exact order (the well-known dotted convention is MIT's department.number, which is the uncertain row `unc-mit-dot-number`, not this). Authored as `proposal` so the shape exists for Joseph to keep or drop — see NEEDS-JOSEPH. The extension stoplist is mandatory for this row: a numerically named file with an uppercase extension (`4300.PDF`) is exactly this shape.
entries.extension_stoplist_note: uppercase spellings of common file extensions — the shape `4300.PDF` is a numerically named file, not a course. The list is extendable data; an uppercase extension it misses is the priced-in residual risk of this row's `proposal` status (NUMBERS is seven letters and outside the {2,5} pattern anyway; it is listed for readers, not for the regex).
entries.design_cite: dispatch prompt §B (no design sentence names this shape)
entries.false_friends: filenames with uppercase extensions (`4300.PDF` — extension stoplist), legal citations (`1983.SCOTUS`-style informal cites), decimal-plus-unit strings (`1000.USD`)
entries.source: dispatch prompt; no external registrar source found (RESEARCH.md)

refused.rationale: The design's worked sparse file. `HW 3` is a work-type clue — homework-ness — never a course code: the design resolves it through grouping context, explicitly not by minting a course fact from the name. The shape is doubly excluded here: HW is stoplisted and {3,4} refuses one- and two-digit numbers. It belongs to the deferred work-type value evidence, not to this file.
refused.quote: the homework may have a homework-like name

refused.rationale: A03's first forbidden value. The five-digit block is why every entry above stops at {3,4}: widening to {3,5} would make each mailing address a course candidate, and no context check should be asked to carry that. ZIP codes are also a named non-date in catalogue 12/04.

Never a course without its department block. The design's date section names the failure class — year-shaped numbers that are course identifiers, versions, builds, ZIPs — and the same ambiguity runs the other way: a bare number is not a course either. A bare number is never-alone by construction in this file because no entry matches one.

A03's second forbidden value class, and the reason shape alone can never validate: `RTX 4090` is lexically a perfect DEPT-space-number. There is no shape that separates device models from course codes, so the defense is layered — context required (a receipt has no floor term), the §3.7 margin, and A03 as the standing acceptance test. Recorded as refused so nobody 'fixes' the overlap by widening the stoplist into a product catalogue.

refused.pattern_label: issue numbers, build numbers, release candidates, revisions
refused.rationale: Issue and build references are the dispatch's named false-friend class for course codes. `#1234` and `build 4300` fail every entry shape (no uppercase letter block / lowercase). `PR 1234` passes ccf-dept-space-number's shape and PR is deliberately NOT stoplisted (PR is a plausible subject block at some institutions); the context check plus the improbability of floor terms in changelogs carry it, and the residual risk is documented on that entry.
refused.design_cite: 00 §3.10 (build numbers as a named confusable class)

refused.rationale: One letter is not a department. The design's own residual example is a boarding-gate screenshot — Gate B12 — and B12 is also a vitamin, A380 an aircraft, C3 a spreadsheet cell. Every entry requires {2,5} letters for exactly this reason.

uncertain.rationale: MIT's convention is real and famous, but the shape is indistinguishable from software versions (3.12), section references (3.10 — this repo's own locators), decimals, and chapter.section numbers. A Python course syllabus containing 'Python 3.12' beside 'credits' would validate course = 3.12 under any honest reading of pattern+context. If wanted, it needs stronger guards than this file can state: zone restriction (filename/title/heading only), an explicit MIT-context gazetteer hit, and margin. Left unauthored pending corpus evidence.

Some registrars use five digits. Admitting {5} makes every `MA 02139`-style address a candidate and hands the whole defense to the stoplist and context. Excluded from v1; needs corpus evidence that five-digit courses appear in the user's files at a rate that justifies the ZIP collision.

Real filenames are often lowercase, and the case-sensitive rule above misses them. A zone-conditional policy — case-insensitive matching in the `filename` zone only, with the stoplist checked case-insensitively too — would recover them at the cost of admitting `march2010.pdf`-style names as candidates. This is a fork for Joseph: per-zone case policy is mechanism, and this file only records the data cost of each choice.

uncertain.pattern: (EN, BS, PS, MA as department blocks)
uncertain.pattern_label: two-letter blocks that are also standard abbreviations
uncertain.rationale: EN 1090 is a European standard and EN 101 an English course; BS 5950 a British Standard and BS a business-school prefix; PS 101 political science and PS 2 a problem set or a PlayStation (single digit — shape-excluded); MA 02139 a ZIP (five digits — shape-excluded) and MA 4300 a maths module. None is stoplisted, because each is a real department somewhere; each is recorded so the collision is visible when tuning weights. The {3,4} digit rule already separates the worst cases.

Cross-listed courses (`ECE/CS 552`) and King's-style module codes (`4CCS1FC1`) exist but each institution's compound grammar differs; a generic compound pattern would be an over-match engine. The simple entries above already match the components (`CS 552`). Left to corpus evidence.

sourcing_note: The five-digit exception was verified by web survey 2026-08-22 against the Notre Dame registrar's course-numbering page; the remaining conventions (2–5-letter subject codes, attached UK/AU forms such as COMP0034/COMP1511) are general-knowledge anchors recorded in RESEARCH.md, not survey findings. The DCF collision is catalogue 04's own finding, reused. No entry names a real course; examples use the design's values (BUSIB 4300, PHYS1401) and public course codes only as format witnesses.
